t.4.31.1: Having heard the words of Aṅgada, and having heard that Lakṣmaṇa was angry, the self-possessed Sugrīva, together with his ministers, rose from his seat.
t.4.31.2: Having weighed what was weighty and what was slight, he who was skilled in counsel and firmly grounded in deliberations spoke these words to his ministers, who were themselves versed in counsel.
t.4.31.3: There is nothing ill-spoken by me, nor anything ill-done by me; I wonder why Lakṣmaṇa, the brother of Rāghava, is angry.
t.4.31.4: The younger brother of Rāghava has been made to hear of faults in me that do not exist, told by my ill-wishers and enemies, who are ever watching for a weak point.
t.4.31.5: In this matter, then, his intention must be found out by all of you, each according to your own judgement and in the proper manner, thoroughly and with care, little by little.
t.4.31.6: Indeed, I have no fear of Lakṣmaṇa, nor even of Rāghava; but a friend angered without cause surely gives rise to alarm.
t.4.31.7: Making a friend is in every way easy, but keeping the friendship is hard; because minds are inconstant, affection is broken even over a trifle.
t.4.31.8: For this reason I am afraid: the kindness that the great-souled Rāma has done for me, I am unable to repay.
t.4.31.9: Thus addressed by Sugrīva, Hanumān, the bull among monkeys, spoke according to his own reasoning in the midst of the monkey ministers.
t.4.31.10: It is in no way surprising, O lord of the monkey hosts, that you do not forget the auspicious and most affectionate kindness that was done for you.
t.4.31.11: But it was for your sake that the heroic Rāghava, casting fear far aside, slew Vālī, whose valour was equal to Śakra's.
t.4.31.12: Rāghava is in every way angered out of affection; there is no doubt about this. He has sent his brother Lakṣmaṇa, the enhancer of prosperity.
t.4.31.14: The sky, its planets and stars now spotless, is free of clouds, which have vanished; and all the quarters are clear and serene, and so are the rivers and the lakes.
t.4.31.13: Heedless as you are, you do not perceive the time, O best of those who know the measures of time; yet the auspicious autumn has set in, dark with blossoming saptacchada trees.
t.4.31.15: O bull among monkeys, you do not perceive that the time for undertaking the campaign has arrived. Clearly it is because you have been heedless that Lakṣmaṇa has come here.
t.4.31.16: The harsh words of the great-souled Rāghava, who is distressed and whose wife has been carried off, delivered to you through another man, should be patiently endured by you.
t.4.31.18: A king must of necessity be told what is beneficial by the ministers he has appointed; for this very reason, casting aside fear, I speak these well-considered words.
t.4.31.19: For Rāghava, when enraged, raising his bow, is capable of bringing under his control the whole world together with the Devas, Asuras and Gandharvas.
t.4.31.17: Indeed, for those who have given offense, I see nothing else fitting but to join the palms in reverence and win the favor of Lakṣmaṇa.
t.4.31.20: He whom one would afterwards have to appease again is not one who should be provoked to anger, especially by a grateful person who remembers a former kindness.
t.4.31.21: Bowing your head to him, together with your son and your friends, O king, abide by your own pledge and remain under his control, as a wife remains under her husband's.
t.4.31.22: The command of Rāma and of Rāma's younger brother, binding upon the lord of the monkeys, must not be set aside by you even in thought; for your mind will come to know the human might of this one, together with Rāghava, whose splendour equals that of the lord of the gods.
